Hi Lina — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attaching a concise MAP + a token-assumptions workbook for procurement. 

Summary of assumptions (model variant: open-llama-13b-quantized-v2, hosted):
- Avg tokens/request (prompt + system): 450 tokens
- Avg tokens/response (generation): 1,100 tokens
- Avg tokens per interaction: 1,550 tokens
- Effective tokens billed: Redwood bills per-token for generation + prompt; the workbook includes per-endpoint breakdown.

Caching & batching:
- Server-side caching: prefix/KV cache is enabled by default for the hosted API for repeated prompts within a session. This reduces effective generation tokens when similar context repeats.
- Client-side: we recommend client-side grouping for prefetch (if you can predict next-turn prompts) but it's optional.
- Batching: Continuous batching in the runtime aggregates compatible requests on the GPU. In hosted tier, batching is automatic up to latency SLOs; recommended batch target for your traffic profile is 8-12 concurrent requests to maximize GPU fill while keeping 95th pct latency under 300ms.

Quantization & model variant tradeoffs:
- open-llama-13b-quantized-v2 uses int8 kernels with ~1.8x throughput improvement vs fp16 and ~8-12% quality delta on medical Qs versus fp16. We included a sensitivity column in the workbook showing tokens/$ delta with quant vs fp16.

Unit econ sensitivity (short):
- Low: 1k DAU, 1 interaction/day => ~1.55M tokens/day => ~46.5M tokens/month
- Mid: 10k DAU, 1.5 interactions/day => ~23.25M tokens/day => ~697.5M tokens/month
- High: 50k DAU, 2 interactions/day => ~155M tokens/day => ~4.65B tokens/month
Per-token price shown in workbook; with our recommended batching/cache profile the per-1M-token effective cost reduces by ~12-18% vs no-batch baseline (workbook includes exact formulas).

Attached: MAP_v1.pdf (milestones + gating), MAP_token_assumptions.xlsx (calc sheet).

Next steps I propose: 
- Rishi to provide a short ops checklist (security/compliance preflight) by Thu 17 Sep
- We finalize SOW and pricing appendix once Procurement confirms acceptable token bands and SLA
- Signaling point for production readiness: acceptance = successful 1-week pilot with <1% error rate, 95th pct latency <350ms, and measured tokens/$ within 15% of MAP projections.

Happy to run a 30-min run-through with Procurement and your infra lead. When are they available?

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi — quick answers and agreed next steps below.

1) Batching-constrained sensitivity: included as a separate tab in MAP_token_assumptions.xlsx ("low-concurrency"). In short: with concurrency = 2-3 the effective tokens/$ worsens by ~28-34% vs our recommended 8-12 concurrency baseline; this is driven by lower GPU utilization and increased per-request kernel overhead.

2) Caching reduction: our measurements on health-domain prompts show median token reduction of 18% after 2 repeated similar prompts and ~25-30% after 3+ repeats when prefix/KV hits occur. We put conservative ranges in the workbook (15-28%).

3) Metering endpoint: yes — hosted exposes a /v1/metrics/tokens endpoint (read-only API key for pilots) that returns daily token counts + breakdown by endpoint. We can enable a pilot key scoped to your project; procurement/ops can poll hourly or integrate with your internal monitoring.

SOW/payment split: 50/40/10 is acceptable. No amended MSA required for the pilot; we'll include the payment split in the SOW appendix and standard MSA terms will apply. If you need a separate PO, send it to finance@redwood.com.
